subject: Post-call: interoperability lab & quant A/B benchmark plan with NovaApps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@novaapps.com>, SaaS Procurement <procure@novaapps.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: interoperability lab & quant A/B benchmark plan with NovaApps

Hi Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a concrete plan to kick off the interoperability benchmark you requested. High-level goals we agreed on: compare Redwood hosted inference vs. the hyperscaler-managed endpoint (HyperscalerX) across latency and steady-state throughput for your 256-token assistant workload, capture p95/p99 tail latencies and tokens/sec under realistic concurrency, and validate quantized variants (int8) vs FP16 for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Scope / deliverables
- A/B runs: Redwood hosted (r-hosted) vs HyperscalerX managed endpoint (h-managed)
- Metric set: p50/p95/p99 latency for 256-token prompts, cold-start 95/99, steady-state tokens/sec, error rates and tail anomalies
- Configs: FP16 baseline, int8 quantized profile (our recommended quant profile), batching at 64ms target latency, concurrency sweep (1, 4, 8, 16)
- Artifacts: runbook + scripts (attached), sample workload (attached), results template (attached), raw logs for your review

Proposed test plan and timeline
- Monday (11/6): Redwood team kicks off staging runs; Dev Patel to run Redwood-hosted A/B matrix and collect baseline numbers (2-hour warmup + 30-minute steady-state per config)
- Tuesday (11/7): HyperscalerX runs (Jordan to coordinate team access)
- Wednesday (11/8): Results consolidation + quick sync to review p95/p99 deltas and tokens/sec differences

What we need from you
- A test account or API key for the HyperscalerX managed endpoint (sandbox creds are fine) and any IP allowlist requirements
- Confirmation of expected RPS pattern (burst vs constant) — if you can share a short trace or the first 5k lines of production requests that would be ideal
- Any SLO thresholds to prioritize (e.g., "p99 < 750ms" or similar)

Attachments: redwood-interop-bench-plan.pdf, sample-workload-256-1k.jsonl, results-template.xlsx

If that timeline looks good I’ll have Dev start the runs on Monday and will loop Jordan in for the Hyperscaler side.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@novaapps.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 16:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: interoperability lab & quant A/B benchmark plan with NovaApps

Thanks Irene — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications before you start:

- Can you include cold-start measurements for a 0->warm transition (we care about the first 10 requests after a long idle period)?
- For tokens/sec please report steady-state mean and 95% CI over the 30-minute window; give samples at 1s granularity if possible
- HyperscalerX team needs a list of IPs to allowlist for your test harness — can you provide that?

I’ll drop a sandbox key to procure@novaapps.com in a separate email (procurement looped here for visibility). We should be able to provide a short trace of typical traffic by EOD Monday.

Appreciate the plan — please go ahead with Redwood-hosted runs on Monday. Keep procurement on the loop for any procurement/PO items.

Cheers,
Alex
Head of AI Engineering, NovaApps

On Fri, Nov 3, 2028 at 3:12 PM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex / Procurement team —
> 
> Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a concrete plan to kick off the interoperability benchmark you requested...

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: NovaApps bench runbook + responsibilities (A/B matrix)

Jordan / Dev — quick coordination email before we run:

Matrix and responsibilities
- Dev: run Redwood-hosted matrix (FP16, int8) across concurrencies [1,4,8,16]. Use batching window 64ms and record p50/95/99 and tokens/sec at 1s resolution. Warmup: 2 hours; steady-state: 30 minutes. Save raw logs to s3://redwood-internal/novaapps/DEAL-9823/runs/
- Jordan: prepare HyperscalerX sandbox creds and run equivalent matrix on their managed endpoint; confirm any per-request headers they require. Coordinate IP allowlist with NovaApps procurement (Alex cc'd).
- Measurement notes: compute p99 from end-to-end latency (request -> last token emitted). For tokens/sec, use total tokens emitted / steady-state duration and also rolling 30s window to catch drops.

Test variants
- Baseline: FP16 with no quantization (Redwood FP16 vs HyperscalerX FP16)
- Variant: Redwood int8 quantized profile (our recommended int8-config) vs HyperscalerX nearest equivalent (note: there may be architecture differences; annotate when comparing)

Deliverables and timing
- Dev: run and upload raw outputs + filled results-template.xlsx by Mon 11/6 5pm PT
- Jordan: HyperscalerX runs by Tue 11/7 EOD PT
- I’ll consolidate Wednesday morning for a 30-min sync with Alex to walk results

Edge cases: include a 5-minute cold-start run (10 cold requests) and a 1-minute spike test at 3x target RPS. Flag any error >1%.

Confirm you both have the attachments from my original note. Ping if any blockers.

Thanks,
Irene

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@novaapps.com>, SaaS Procurement <procure@novaapps.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Confirmed: NovaApps interoperability bench schedule + artifacts attached

Alex / procurement — quick confirmation following our internal prep:

- Redwood-hosted runs: started today (11/6) and will finish by 5pm PT. Dev will upload outputs to the Drive link and S3 bucket.
- HyperscalerX runs: Jordan will execute on Tue 11/7 once we receive the sandbox key; please send sandbox key to procure@novaapps.com and cc jordan.blake@redwood.com
- Attachments: redwood-interop-bench-plan.pdf (runbook), sample-workload-256-1k.jsonl (request samples), results-template.xlsx (reporting template) are attached and available at https://drive.google.com/redwood/novaapps/bench-plan

Next steps for you:
- Send the HyperscalerX sandbox key and allowlist contact (we’ll provide IPs shortly)
- Share the traffic trace when available (helps us model burstiness)

Expect the consolidated deck and a short 30-minute results call on Wed 11/8 morning PT. If you prefer a different slot, we can flex.

Thanks — looking forward to getting concrete numbers across p95/p99 and tokens/sec so you can make a call on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
